problem.title: An IPO can look simple until you actually try to understand it.
problem.description: The information may be available, but it can be fragmented across technical documents, announcements, commentary and social media. The challenge is knowing what matters, what is verified, and how the pieces fit together.

points.title: Too much information
points.text: Important information can be spread across prospectuses, announcements, financial statements and other sources.

points.title: Too much jargon
points.text: Terms such as offer price, allotment, dilution, valuation and subscription can make the process feel harder than it needs to be.

points.title: Too much noise
points.text: Social media commentary, repeated claims and market excitement are not substitutes for verification and analysis.

points.title: Too many unanswered questions
points.text: What are you actually buying? What does it cost? What are the risks? How does subscription work? What happens after allotment?

promise.title: Clarity without the hype.
promise.description: This book is designed to help you build understanding and judgment—not to tell you what decision to make.
points: Understand IPO terminology in plain language.
Understand what shares represent and what ownership means.
Read an offer document with a structured framework.
Evaluate the business, financials, valuation and risks.
Understand subscription, allotment and ownership mechanics.
Prepare the questions and calculations that matter.
Recognize behavioral traps such as FOMO and herd behavior.
Separate facts from interpretations, examples and scenarios.

faq.title: Questions you may have.
faq.description: A few important things to know before getting the guide.

items.question: Is this book telling me whether I should buy the IPO?
items.answer: No. The guide is designed for financial education, evaluation and preparation. It does not provide individualized buy, sell or participation recommendations.

items.question: Is this only for experienced investors?
items.answer: No. The book is specifically designed to make IPO concepts accessible to beginners while still providing practical evaluation frameworks.

items.question: What will I learn about the Dangote Refinery IPO?
items.answer: The guide uses the Dangote Refinery IPO as a real-world case study for understanding IPO structure, offer information, business evaluation, financials, valuation, risks, subscription, allotment, ownership and monitoring.

items.question: Will the book guarantee returns or allocation?
items.answer: No. No return, allocation, price appreciation or financial outcome is guaranteed.

items.question: Does the book explain IPO terminology?
items.answer: Yes. It covers important terms relating to IPOs, shares, ownership, markets, financial statements, valuation, subscription, allotment and post-IPO ownership.

items.question: Does it include practical tools?
items.answer: Yes. The framework includes checklists, calculations, evaluation tools, a glossary, questions and preparation frameworks.

items.question: What if official IPO information changes?
items.answer: Time-sensitive information should always be checked against the relevant current authoritative source. The book's framework is designed to remain useful even when live offer details change.
